claims.text: Formation of a stable solid-solution phase influences the elevated-temperature stress-strain behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
Formation of a stable solid-solution phase influences the elevated-temperature thermal expansion of HfNbTaTiZr.
Formation of a stable solid-solution phase influences the elevated-temperature elastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
A stable solid-solution phase enhances the mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr.
A stable solid-solution phase enhances the thermal stability of HfNbTaTiZr.
Heat treatment near 1000°C for approximately 1 hour promotes formation of a stable solid-solution phase in HfNbTaTiZr.
Elevated temperature activates atomic diffusion and rearrangement in HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermally activated diffusion and atomic rearrangement enhance the mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermally activated diffusion and atomic rearrangement enhance the thermal stability of HfNbTaTiZr.
Heat-treated HfNbTaTiZr will have greater strength than an untreated as-cast or wrought baseline.
Heat-treated HfNbTaTiZr will have greater ductility than an untreated as-cast or wrought baseline.
Heat-treated HfNbTaTiZr will have an improved thermal expansion coefficient relative to an untreated baseline.
The proposed response applies from 500°C to 1200°C at strain rates from 10^-4 s^-1 to 10^-2 s^-1.
The proposed hypothesis is bounded at 1200°C and 20% strain.
